data.description:
Über uns

Türen öffnen oder Deals abschließen? Bei uns machst du beides!
Unser Vertrieb ist bereit für den nächsten Schritt, und wir suchen die Person, die ihn mit uns geht. Du gehst aktiv auf mittelständische Unternehmen zu, erkennst ihre digitalen Herausforderungen und entwickelst gemeinsam mit unseren Expert:innen aus Strategie, UX/UI, Entwicklung, digitalem Marketing und KI Lösungen, die für unsere Kund:innen einen messbaren Unterschied machen. Dabei bist du nicht einfach „nur" Verkäufer:in, sondern Gesprächspartner:in und Berater:in auf Augenhöhe. Wenn du lieber Chancen schaffst, als auf Anfragen zu warten, freuen wir uns dich kennen zu lernen!


Das gibt es zu tun

Als Netzwerker:in im strategischen Neukundengeschäft:

  • Du gewinnst strategisch relevante Neukund:innen über dein persönliches Netzwerk, Empfehlungen, Veranstaltungen und gezielte Direktansprache von Entscheider:innen
  • Qualifizierte Termine aus unserem Sales Development übernimmst du, vertiefst die Bedarfsanalyse und entwickelst daraus konkrete Opportunities
  • Gemeinsam mit unserem SDR definierst du Zielgruppen und Wunschkunden und sorgst für eine reibungslose Übergabe vom ersten Kontakt bis zum Abschluss

Als Berater:in und Closer:in:
  • Du berätst zu digitalen Lösungen – vom Website-Relaunch über individuelle Softwareprojekte bis hin zu KI-Produkten – und übersetzt technische Zusammenhänge in greifbaren Business-Nutzen
  • Du entwickelst gemeinsam mit unseren Fachteams Lösungskonzepte, Kalkulationen und Angebote
  • Du präsentierst Angebote, führst Verhandlungen und bringst Projekte eigenverantwortlich zum Abschluss
  • Du baust nachhaltige Beziehungen zu unseren Kund:innen auf.
Und im Tagesgeschäft:
  • Du entwickelst unsere Bestandskund:innen aktiv weiter und identifizierst Cross- und Upselling-Potenziale
  • Du beobachtest Markttrends, insbesondere im KI-Bereich, und leitest aktiv Ideen zur Weiterentwicklung unserer Sales-Strategie ab.
  • Du steuerst deine Aktivitäten zielorientiert entlang klarer Vertriebs-KPIs – von Kontakten über Termine und Opportunities bis zum Auftragseingang
  • Du pflegst Kontakte, Aktivitäten und Opportunities konsequent in unserem CRM und weißt jederzeit, welche nächsten Schritte anstehen
  • Du arbeitest eng mit Marketing, Consulting und unseren Produktionsteams zusammen und bringst Impulse aus dem Markt direkt ins Team


Das bringst Du mit

  • Mehrjährige Erfahrung im B2B-Vertrieb erklärungsbedürftiger digitaler Dienstleistungen oder Lösungen – idealerweise im Agenturumfeld – und nachweisbare Vertriebserfolge.
  • Erfahrung darin, den gesamten Vertriebsprozess selbstständig zu führen: vom Erstkontakt über Beratung und Angebot bis zur Verhandlung und zum Abschluss.
  • „Hunter-Mentalität“: Du gehst gerne aktiv auf Menschen zu und brauchst keine fertigen Leads, um erfolgreich zu sein.
  • Fundiertes Verständnis in mehreren dieser Themen: Websites, Relaunches und CMS/DXP, UX/UI, digitales Marketing, Webentwicklung und Webtechnologien oder Individuelle Software-Entwicklung sowie Apps, APIs und Systemintegrationen – zusätzliches Know-how rund um KI, Chatbots und KI-Agenten ist ein Plus.
  • Du musst kein:e Entwickler:in sein - aber du sprichst mit Entwickler:innen auf Augenhöhe und kannst gleichzeitig einer Geschäftsführung erklären, welchen Nutzen eine Lösung bringt.
  • Strukturierte, eigenverantwortliche und ergebnisorientierte Arbeitsweise und Routine im Umgang mit CRM-Systemen - Zuverlässigkeit ist dabei einer deiner wichtigsten Werte.
  • Idealerweise setzt du KI-Tools bereits aktiv im Vertriebsalltag ein, z. B. für Recherche, Gesprächsvorbereitung oder Angebotserstellung.
  • Überzeugungskraft, Verbindlichkeit und den Willen, Ergebnisse zu verantworten: Du wartest nicht auf Chancen, du erzeugst sie.
  • Gültige Fahrerlaubnis (Führerschein Klasse B) und Reisebereitschaft
  • Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift sowie eine klare, professionelle und sympathische Ausdrucksweise


Das bekommst Du

  • Start & Welcoming so wie du es verdienst! Ein strukturiertes Onboarding mit echten Ansprechpersonen - damit du vom ersten Tag an durchstartest.
  • Remote Work: Homeoffice innerhalb von Deutschland oder Arbeiten in unserem modernen Büro in Offenburg? Arbeite so, wie es für dich am besten passt.
  • AI-first arbeiten, statt darüber zu reden: Lizenzen für Vusyon, Claude, Chat-GPT, Copilot & Co. stellen wir. Neue Tools und Modelle darfst du ausprobieren - und deine Erkenntnisse verändern, wie das ganze Team arbeitet. 
  • Betriebliche Altersvorsorge mit 20 % Arbeitgeberzuschuss - deutlich über dem gesetzlichen Standard.
  • Du entscheidest ob Hansefit-Mitgliedschaft oder 50 € monatlich per Spendit Card - dein Benefit, deine Wahl.
  • Urlaub, der mit dir wächst: 30 Tage Jahresurlaub + dazu Weihnachten und Silvester frei - und mit steigender Betriebszugehörigkeit kommen weitere Tage dazu. 
  • Jobticket oder JobRad - wir machen deinen Weg ins Office einfacher und grüner.
  • Feiern gehört dazu - Quarterly Allhands Events, Sommerfest, Weihnachtsfeier oder einfach so - wir wissen, wie man Korken knallen lässt.
  • Ein Team, das wirklich zählt. Flache Hierarchien, schnelle Entscheidungen und ein offenes Ohr auch für das, was dich persönlich bewegt.


Das sind WIR

Transformation ist für uns kein Trend, sondern unser Auftrag: Seit 1995 begleitet die avenit Group Unternehmen dabei, sich für die digitale Zukunft neu aufzustellen - ganzheitlich, strategisch und mit klarem Blick für nachhaltige Erfolge. Mit avenit und Vusyon vereinen wir zwei starke Kräfte - langjährige führende Digitalexpertise und modernste KI-Technologie - zu einem Partner für maßgeschneiderte Lösungen, die wirklich funktionieren. Wir glauben daran, dass nachhaltiger Erfolg auf Augenhöhe entsteht; im echten Dialog mit unseren Kunden. Unsere 60 Kolleg:innen lassen diese Vision jeden Tag zur Realität werden. Werde Teil eines Teams, das Zukunft nicht nur denkt, sondern gestaltet.

data.title: Java Backend Developer (m/w/d)

data.description:
New Challenge

About Us 
Project Q GmbH ("Q") is a Germany-based DefenseTech company with offices in Berlin and Munich. We network market-available sensors, effectors, or situational awareness systems into a tactical IoT backbone that reliably provides armed forces and security agencies with cross-domain information superiority — automated, scalable, and cost-efficient.

Our solutions integrate seamlessly into existing defense and maritime infrastructures, delivering fast data fusion and AI-enhanced analytics for robust situational awareness in dynamic environments. We build platform-agnostic systems that enable real interoperability across domains.

As a Staff Software Engineer, you'll directly impact the technical direction of our orchestration products – Hydris – the coordination engine for sensors and mission systems, and the interoperability API that underpins it. 

You'll work at the layer where heterogeneous real-world systems like radars, AIS receivers, LoRa mesh radios, satellite feeds, and C2 platforms become a single coherent picture. The problems lie in distributed systems, protocols, and data modeling areas. They play out in environments that are bandwidth-constrained, intermittently connected, and operationally unforgiving. 

The role is deeply hands-on, but it expects you to shape what we build and how we build it, not just deliver what's specified.

What you'll do
Core engine development

  • Design and build the systems that power Hydris.
  • Go is your primary language. You should be comfortable reading Rust and TypeScript across the codebase, even if you're not writing in them day-to-day.
  • Own the architecture of a system that must run reliably on edge hardware, in disconnected mesh networks, and at scale — often all of that simultaneously.
Protocol and integration architecture
  • Evolve the schema that defines how every sensor, asset, and mission system talks to Hydris.
  • Make API design decisions that hold up across our client libraries without creating a maintenance burden.
  • Continue refining the integration framework that lets Hydris connect to new sensor types, data sources, and command systems.
  • Set the patterns for how built-in integrations (ADS-B, AIS, ASTERIX, Meshtastic, SpaceTrack, TAK, federation) are structured, tested, and maintained.
  • Make it straightforward for external developers and system vendors to build their own plugins/integrations to Hydris.
Distributed systems
  • Architect the peer-to-peer mesh and federation layer that keeps Hydris operational in disconnected, denied, intermittent, and limited-bandwidth environments.
  • Solve the hard coordination problems: conflict resolution across federated nodes, eventual consistency of entity state, and track correlation across unreliable links.
  • Ensure the system degrades gracefully rather than failing completely when connectivity is lost or constrained.
Technical leadership
  • Set technical standards for the codebase: how we test distributed behavior, how we handle protocol versioning, how we think about backward compatibility in an API-first product.
  • Review code with a focus on long-term maintainability and operational correctness, not just feature completion.
  • Make build-versus-integrate decisions and help the team clearly understand the trade-offs.

You should apply if you
  • Have built and shipped distributed systems that run in production, ideally in environments where reliability matters more than convenience.
  • Are comfortable working across the stack, from Protobuf schema design and systems-level Go, to the TypeScript that puts a map in front of a user.
  • Have well-formed views about API design and protocol evolution, informed by experience maintaining APIs that other people depend on.
  • Can operate effectively with a high degree of autonomy but are adept at collaboration with colleagues toward high-quality technical decisions, at scale.
  • Are interested in contributing to European military, maritime, and critical infrastructure defence systems.
  • Write clearly and communicate architectural decisions in a way that survives beyond the conversation where they were made. 
  • Working language is English. German is not required.
You'd be a great fit with
  • Experience with geospatial systems, sensor fusion, or track management.
  • Familiarity with defense or ISR data standards like CoT/TAK, ASTERIX, SAPIENT, MIL-STD-2525.
  • Background in networking, mesh architectures, or systems designed for contested or degraded communication environments.
  • Experience working on developer-facing open-source infrastructure where adoption depends on the quality of the API and documentation.

We Offer
  • Remote work anywhere in Germany, or hybrid/on-site in Berlin or Munich if you're already based there and prefer an office.
  • High degree of autonomy and ownership, a flat structure, and real input into technical direction.
  • Annual €1500 Learning & development budget (available after probation).
  • Bike Leasing and Urban Sports Club membership.
  • 30 days of paid time off.
Note: We're unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role – candidates must already be eligible to work in Germany.

data.title: Staff/Senior Software Engineer - Hydris - Golang (d/f/m)

data.description:
New Challenge

About Us
Project Q GmbH ("Q") is a defence technology company with offices in Berlin and Munich, and a trusted partner of the German Armed Forces. Our customers field sensors, drones and C2 systems from many vendors that were never built to work together. We build Hydris, an orchestration layer that integrates the systems they already field, and the ones they'll add next, into one picture operators can act on across defence, public safety, and critical infrastructure. Hydris runs at the edge, keeps working when the link drops, and its core is open source under Apache 2.0.

As Senior Product Manager for Mission Devices, you'll own the hardware that puts Hydris in the field. 

You'll work end-to-end, from discovery with operators through hardware build cycles to fielded units, and you'll decide what gets built rather than work through someone else's backlog. The bar is concrete: devices that run for months off-grid in contested RF environments.

What you'll do
Discovery and requirements

  • Spend time with end users in their operating environment to understand their workflows in depth, not just their stated requirements.
  • Validate assumptions about value, usability, feasibility and viability through prototypes, bench tests and field trials before committing to hardware fabrication.
  • Analyze contractual specifications with Program Managers, separating firm constraints from areas where there's room for the best technical solution.
Roadmap and delivery
  • Maintain an outcome-focused roadmap aligned to hardware build cycles (EVT/DVT/PVT), firmware releases and OTA update pipelines.
  • Define requirements and field metrics for each device, including detection performance, energy efficiency, mission endurance and SWaP, and make the trade-offs between them.
  • Prioritize investment across the device family, deciding where to extend existing devices and where a new one is needed.
Systems and interoperability
  • Make sure devices integrate with Hydris as and interoperate with third-party systems through industry standards and protocols.
  • Design provisioning, commissioning and deployment workflows that are simple and reliable in the field.
  • Investigate issues that span hardware, firmware and communications, and work with engineering to resolve them.
Collaboration
  • Act as the main source of product context and the product's champion, making sure the team, leadership and customers understand what we're building and why.
  • Work in a product trio with engineering (hardware and ML) and design. 
  • Partner with Program and Capture Managers to keep the product vision aligned with contractual commitments.
  • Write clear PRDs and decision records, and mentor teammates on discovery practice and hardware–software trade-offs.

You should apply if you have
  • 5+ years of product management experience with hardware–software products, for example in embedded systems, IoT, robotics, defence systems or edge AI.
  • Experience taking a connected hardware product from EVT/DVT through production into operational use, including in-field updates.
  • Experience running product development end to end, from discovery to engineering-ready work, and the ability to adapt to however a team works.
  • Ability making decisions with incomplete information, and the judgment to know when a decision is risky enough to slow down.
  • Clear communication with hardware engineers, ML researchers and operators alike.
  • Motivation to contribute to European security and sovereignty.
  • Willingness to travel regularly to military exercises, test ranges and customer sites in Germany and NATO partner countries, sometimes in demanding field conditions.
  • Eligibility for German security clearance (SÜ2).
  • Fluency in German and English (C1 or higher).
You'd be a particularly great fit with
  • A degree in electrical, mechanical or systems engineering, robotics or a related field, or equivalent hands-on experience bringing hardware products from prototype to production.
  • Experience in military, public safety or other mission-critical operational environments.
  • Exposure to sensor fusion, mesh networking or degraded RF environments, including familiarity with interoperability standards such as Cursor on Target, SAPIENT, ONVIF or ASTERIX.

We Offer
  • Direct feedback from the field: you'll see the products you build tested in real operating environments by the people who use them.
  • Prime Berlin-Mitte location – right between Alexanderplatz and Hackescher Markt.
  • High degree of autonomy and ownership, and flat structure.
  • Annual €1500 Learning & development budget  (available after probation).
  • Bike Leasing and Urban Sports Club membership.
  • 30 days of paid time off.

Note: We're unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role – candidates must already be eligible to work in Germany.

Intro

As our Health Claims lead, you'll own claims decisions on Feather's health MGA books from day one: coverage, declines, settlement amounts, all within policy terms. You'll manage our insurance carrier relationships, decide how we work with service providers, and build the playbook, automations and systems that let the function scale as we grow MGA health claims fast across expat and international health.

At Feather, we're building insurance that actually matters to our customers. It rests on three principles: a fully digital experience, modern and flexible plans, and reliable human support. And because we build it all for expats living abroad, we're a genuinely different kind of insurer.


Why work at Feather?

  • We're small, lean, and we love what we do. The usual buzzwords here, except we actually mean them. Staying small helps us focus on what matters, and we want to keep it that way.
  • You'll work on a product that is loved by customers. Our excellent Trustpilot and Google reviews speak for themselves.
  • There's plenty of space to grow. We trust you to take ownership and make real decisions from day one, and you'll have all the support you need to succeed.
  • You'll have the freedom to build something from scratch. You're not inheriting a finished system. You're building the decision logic, reporting, and playbook that let health claims scale.
  • Flexible remote work policy. We offer a remote-first work environment, hiring across Europe via an Employer of Record. We host company retreats, team dinners, and meetups to spend in-person time together.


What you bring to the table

  • You have hands-on experience handling health claims across borders or internationally.
  • You are familiar with medical coding and provider billing.
  • You have an instinct for automation and AI tooling, and you use it daily.
  • You take tough decisions daily, including saying no to customers, and you still enjoy the work.
  • You are pragmatic in an unfinished system: you improve it while running it.
  • You are a fluent English speaker.
Nice to have:
  • German, Spanish, or French language skills.
  • Experience with moratorium underwriting.
  • A medical background.
  • Experience in an MGA or delegated authority setup.
  • Experience managing third-party administrators (TPAs).


You'll be responsible for

  • You will make claims decisions
    • You will interpret coverage, decide declines, settlement amounts, and goodwill within policy terms, with real authority, not recommend-and-wait.
    • You will handle expat and international health claims: cross-border invoices across languages and billing conventions, currency and tax, and coordination with statutory and private cover in the country of residence.
  • You will manage our carrier relationships
    • You will own claims reporting and bordereaux, contentious cases, and coverage disputes with our insurance partners.
    • You will keep audit-ready records throughout, so nothing surprises the carrier.
  • You will decide how we work with service providers
    • You will decide where using third-party administrators (TPAs) makes sense, and manage instructions, quality, turnaround, and commercial performance where we use them.
  • You will build the operating model
    • You will close gaps with product and engineering across intake, documents, decision support, payout, and automation.
    • You will run audits and fraud checks, working toward semi-automated monitoring with the data team.
  • You will build capability
    • You will write the playbook so health claims stops depending on one person.
    • You will train whoever joins the team next.


What will the interview process look like?

  1. CV screening
  2. Initial phone call with our People team. We'll have a chat and get to know each other (30m)
  3. Hiring manager call. We'll cover the role, skills needed, and answer your questions (1 hour)
  4. Case study. We'll give you a case study to work on, which will give you an idea of the type of projects you'd take on at Feather (3-4h)
  5. Case study discussion. We'll go through your reasoning and approach together (90min)
  6. Call with our Head of Ops. We'll talk through our async, remote-first way of working and how our team operates day to day (45min)
  7. Final interview. You'll be speaking to one member of our leadership team (45min)


Does this sound like a good fit for you? Apply now!

At Feather, we actively foster inclusive representation within our teams and embrace a diverse mix of talent. We encourage applicants from all educational paths to apply: we believe that what you’ve built, worked on, and achieved is far more important than on-paper qualifications.

About the team

The Commercial Planning team sits at the heart of SumUp's commercial engine, turning complex data into the financial insight that shapes how we grow. We partner closely with Sales leaders and commercial teams to make sure our planning is accurate, proactive, and genuinely useful to the people making decisions. In this role, you'll primarily support our Sales function, owning analytical and planning workstreams while acting as a trusted finance partner to Sales leadership. If you're energised by owning complex models, understanding what drives sales performance, influencing commercial decisions, and being the person stakeholders turn to when they need clarity, this is the role for you.

What you'll do

  • Own end-to-end revenue and customer acquisition budget (CAB) planning for acquisition channels, building scalable financial models, running scenario analyses, and delivering proactive performance insights to senior stakeholders
  • Act as a primary finance business partner to Sales and commercial leaders, building trusted relationships, embedding financial models into decision-making, and using data to challenge assumptions and identify opportunities to improve performance
  • Conduct deep-dive analyses at country, merchant category, and channel level to surface revenue risks and opportunities, and present findings clearly to senior, non-technical audiences
  • Build business cases and product-level revenue forecasts to support existing and new product growth initiatives
  • Contribute to the migration of commercial planning from spreadsheets to scalable forecasting tools, and help reduce manual effort in month-end reporting workflows
  • Provide day-to-day guidance to an intern and/or analyst, helping them develop their skills and navigate complex analytical tasks

You'll be great for this role if…

  • You have experience acting as a primary finance business partner to Sales and commercial leaders, building trusted relationships, embedding financial models into decision-making, and using data to challenge assumptions and identify opportunities to improve performance
  • Expert-level financial modelling skills, including multi-driver models and scenario analysis, with advanced proficiency in Excel or Google Sheets
  • Proven ability to act as a trusted finance business partner, comfortable challenging and influencing Sales leaders and senior commercial stakeholders
  • Working knowledge of SQL for data extraction and manipulation from large datasets
  • Clear and structured communicator, able to translate complex analysis into sharp, actionable insight for senior non-technical audiences
  • Comfort working in fast-moving environments where priorities shift, and structure is still being built

Why you should join SumUp

🌎 Opportunity to work with a truly global, multicultural team from our central London Bridge location, wrapped in historic charm and modern flair. This involves an office-first setup

🌈 Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion: be part of a workplace that values and promotes diversity, fostering an inclusive environment where everyone's perspectives are respected and embraced

Established in 2004, OLIVER is the world's first and only specialist in designing, building, and running bespoke in-house agencies and marketing ecosystems for brands. We partner with over 300 clients in 40+ countries and counting. Our unique model drives creativity and efficiency, allowing us to deliver tailored solutions that resonate deeply with audiences. 

As a part of The Brandtech Group, we're at the forefront of leveraging cutting-edge AI technology to revolutionise how we create and deliver work. Our AI solutions enhance efficiency, spark creativity, and drive insightful decision-making, empowering our teams to produce innovative and impactful results. 

Role: Global Programme Director

Location:  London, United Kingdom (1-3 days a week from our London HQ)

 

THE OPPORTUNITY

OLIVER is growing — and we're building our pipeline of senior programme talent ahead of new account wins across our global network.

We're looking to connect with experienced Global Programme Directors who are open to an early conversation about upcoming opportunities. As we pitch for and win major international accounts, we want to hear from programme leaders who thrive in complex, multi-region environments and have a consistent track record of delivering at scale.

This isn't a specific vacancy. It's an invitation to start a conversation.

Based in London, with a hybrid working pattern (1–3 days in our London offices), these roles sit at the intersection of strategic direction, commercial leadership, and operational excellence. We support flexible working and are open to discussing different arrangements. We offer reasonable adjustments throughout our process.

THE ROLE

Global Programme Directors at OLIVER are the most senior programme voice on their accounts — trusted by clients at executive level and accountable for delivery health, financial performance, and team capability across everything they touch.

You'll lead medium-to-complex, multi-region programmes, bringing together creative, production, technology, and commercial disciplines to deliver transformational outcomes for some of the world's most ambitious brands. You'll drive measurable change within one of the most innovative in-house agency models in the industry — and help shape what programme excellence looks like across OLIVER's global network.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Programme Delivery and Governance

  • Lead medium-to-complex global programmes, maintaining alignment to strategic goals, financial targets, and client expectations throughout
  • Develop and drive programme vision — managing organisational change and delivering integrated outcomes across studios, functions, and geographies
  • Hold full accountability for delivery health: governance, risk management, issue resolution, and stakeholder coordination across concurrent workstreams
  • Establish and track KPIs; produce regular programme status reports covering risks, issues, and performance metrics; implement corrective actions as needed
  • Lead enterprise-scale transformation programmes centred on technology, people, and process — mapping dependencies, managing timelines, and ensuring nothing falls between workstreams

Commercial Leadership

  • Hold full accountability for account gross profit, including all approvals that affect GP: resourcing decisions, freelancers, expenses, and ad hoc cost requirements

Resource and Team Leadership

WHAT YOU BRING

Commercial and Budget Skills

Qualifications: Formal qualifications are welcome but not required. Equivalent experience counts — gained through work, study, or professional development.

At CoMind, we are developing a non-invasive neuromonitoring technology that will result in a new era of clinical brain monitoring. In joining us, you will be helping to create cutting-edge technologies that will improve how we diagnose and treat brain disorders, ultimately improving and saving the lives of patients across the world.

The Role

The Data Science team at CoMind develops the algorithms and machine learning systems that transform raw optical interference signals from CoMind One into continuous, clinically meaningful measurements of cerebral blood flow, intracranial pressure, and autoregulation. Working at the frontier of photonics, physiology, and applied ML, the team's work directly determines what CoMind One can measure, how accurately, and under what clinical conditions.

As Principal Data Scientist, you will be a technical authority for CoMind's data science function, setting methodological direction for signal condition and extraction, personally driving the most complex and highest-impact problems, and providing expert guidance on data science best practice across the team. This is a senior individual contributor role: you will not manage people directly, but your technical leadership will shape how the entire team approaches its most challenging problems. You will work closely with R&D, Clinical, and Software Engineering.

At CoMind, all team members work at least 4 days per week from our new Kings Cross offices, plus a flexible work-from-home day.

Responsibilities:

  • Act as the technical authority for the end-to-end signal processing and inference chain for CoMind’s technologies: from raw optical data through to clinical measurements

  • Set the methodological direction for estimation, signal extraction and ML modelling across the team: which approaches suit which problems, how they are evaluated, and what evidence is required before a method is trusted.

  • Own signal processing and analysis programmes from research through to validated, production-quality implementations with Software Engineering.

  • Derive achievable performance bounds from instrument and noise models, and use them to drive algorithm selection, requirement setting and design trade-offs

  • Own how the team handles uncertainty and calibration — inference methods appropriate to small clinical cohorts, per-patient estimation with quantified uncertainty, and calibration strategies that make measurements comparable across devices, sessions and patients.

  • Set the standard for how the data science function works: reproducibility, analysis and code review, experiment design, dataset governance and ground-truth definitions

  • Act as the primary technical reviewer and expert resource across the research organisation, reviewing technical reports, analysis plans and evaluation methodology, and holding the bar for methodological rigour and scientific integrity.

  • Identify and introduce new, best-practice methods from estimation, inference and measurement science in adjacent fields.

  • Act as a mentor to members of the Data Science teams and across the wider business

  • Contribute to CoMind's IP and publication strategy, authoring and reviewing technical papers, patent applications and regulatory documents.

AI is fundamental to our culture. It's not just a tool, but a core part of how we work, collaborate, and innovate. We expect all team members to embrace AI in their daily work and continuously find new ways to use it effectively.

Skills & Experience:

  • 15+ years of experience in data science, ML, or applied research, with a strong track record of independent technical leadership on complex, ambiguous problems

  • A career working to extract small signals from noisy, complex physiological systems, and developing and deploying physical models of those systems to support those efforts.

  • Deep expertise in physiological time-series signal processing methodologies.

  • A demonstrated ability to take algorithmic work from research concept through to production-quality, validated implementations in shipped product.

  • Designing device performance evaluation methods where no prior gold-standard exists: simulating physical systems, running sensitivity analysis, identifying failure modes, and developing signal processing solutions to address those challenges.

  • Extensive experience owning calibration and cross-instrument comparability work that involved noise models, error budgets, and evaluation of experimental data

  • Strong record of scientific output: publications, patents, or equivalent evidence of original technical contribution and domain authority

Nice to Have:

  • Background in neuroscience, neuromonitoring, or cerebrovascular physiology

  • Experience with optical signal processing - e.g. LiDAR, pulse oximetry, NIRS, laser doppler flowmetry, or related technologies

  • Experience in a regulated industry (medical devices, diagnostics, pharma, or similar), with familiarity of algorithm validation and documentation requirements for software as a medical device

Benefits:

  • Company equity plan so all employees share in the success of the company

  • Salary-sacrifice pension scheme

  • Private medical, dental and vision insurance (medical history disregarded)

  • Group life assurance at 4x annual income

  • Comprehensive mental health support, including unlimited access to 1:1 sessions with trained professionals

  • Unlimited holiday allowance (+ bank holidays) and one week of remote working per quarter

  • Lunch voucher (£10) every day for JustEat and free dinner on those days where you need to work later

  • Twice weekly deliveries of fresh fruit and an extensive selection of snacks and drinks

  • YuLife subscription, allowing you to turn your daily steps and meditation into discounts at a range of stores

  • Access to Udemy for upskilling and professional development


Disclaimer - We use Granola, an AI notetaker, throughout our interview process to help capture notes. It's used only for note-taking during the conversation. Transcripts aren't saved to shared drives or stored externally. Let us know if you'd prefer we don't.

We pull medical technology from the future to solve human health.

 

Scarlet is authorised to assess and certify medical devices. We combine clinical, technical and regulatory expertise with AI agents and software so rigorous certification can keep pace with product development at the world’s most ambitious technology companies, without lowering the safety bar.

Our customers have cut a year or more from their certification timelines for new AI-enabled medical devices and shortened product-update cycles from months to weeks. You’ll join a team building the infrastructure that makes these outcomes repeatable at scale.

About the role

The Applied Machine Learning team owns production systems and pursues new ideas, from conception and prototyping through to deployment, evaluation and iterative improvement.

Working with clinicians, assessors and engineers, we build reliable ML systems that help bring medical devices to market faster, without compromising safety. It’s a domain rich in text, data and expert judgment, with little precedent for much of what we’re building.

You’ll own meaningful problems in how we assess medical devices: define success with domain experts, decide what to build and test, and take ML systems through deployment and measurable improvement in production.

Responsibilities

Things you might work on:

  • Agentic document understanding – Build agents that search, parse and visually inspect messy technical files: scanned certificates, tables, architecture diagrams and thousands of pages of evidence. Find what matters and show exactly where it came from.

  • Harnesses built for evidence – Develop custom agent harnesses for retrieving information across large document collections in varied formats. Preserve source attribution, minimise hallucination, and make deliberate trade-offs between accuracy, latency and cost. Deploy to production.

  • Evals wired into real workflows – Define success with assessors and build datasets and benchmarks that capture a complex, nuanced domain. Measure retrieval quality, citation correctness and agreement with expert judgment alongside the impact on assessor effort, assessment quality and customer experience, including rework. Use the results to choose what to improve next.

  • Applied AI alignment – Build useful agents that respect the impartiality and objectivity required of a certification body. Help people understand the evidence, recognise uncertainty and retain responsibility for consequential judgments.

Who you are

  • Creator of datasets – You roll up your sleeves and build the dataset you wish existed, rather than wait for someone else to give you one.

  • Establisher of evals – You think from first principles about statistics and evaluating ML systems. You're suspicious of benchmarks that don't match reality.

  • Builder of agent systems – You understand deep-learning, agent tools, context management and information retrieval, and how they interact.

  • Shipper of software – 3+ years shipping software to production. You own deployment, monitoring and the investigation when something breaks.

  • Security judgment – You’ve made and implemented pragmatic security decisions for production systems. You can reason about data access, permissions, untrusted inputs and actions with real consequences; design proportionate mitigations; and recognise when specialist review is needed.

  • Systems design – You’ve designed, deployed and operated production systems. You can choose infrastructure that fits the workload, explain the trade-offs in complexity, reliability, security and cost, and work within shared engineering standards.

  • Hacker – You take ambitious projects from concept to reality with whatever tools are at hand. You experiment, measure and change your mind.

  • Builder – You're insatiably curious about real-world problems and care that what you build has clear economic and human value.

  • Owner of ambiguous problems – You can point to an ambiguous problem you owned: working directly with domain experts to define success, choosing what to try, and following it through experiments and production to measurable improvement.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience deploying agent systems with tool use, sensitive data or consequential actions, including evaluating their behaviour and designing safeguards.

  • Experience building retrieval or document-understanding systems whose outputs must be checked against complex source evidence.

Interview process

  1. Intro call with Alan – 30 mins

  2. Technical interview – 60 mins

  3. Working session in our London office with Alan and Jamie – 90 mins

  4. Culture and values interviews with James and Jamie – 2 × 30 mins

THE ROLE

We're looking for an Infrastructure Engineer to build the secure, reliable foundation everyone else at ClaimSorted builds on top of - and the self-service tools to create accurate analytics.

  • You'll close the gaps before they become a headline - own access controls, PII protection, and compliance end-to-end, at a company handling real claims data for the world's largest insurers. This isn't theoretical security work; it's the real thing, with real stakes.

  • You'll standardize how we build and run infrastructure - bring consistency across the stack, build the observability to actually see what's happening, and drive measurable gains in reliability, latency, and cost as we scale.

  • You'll build the data infrastructure that lets teams answer their own questions - accurate, self-service analytics that mean claims and ops don't have to file an engineering ticket and wait days for something they could pull themselves.

We love working together in the office, so this is a full-time, office-based role in our London office. We're a tight-knit team that genuinely enjoys building this together, and we think you'll feel that from day one.

WHO YOU ARE

We care more about hunger and grit than years on a resume. You might come from a platform, security, or data infrastructure background - what matters is you've owned the unglamorous stuff that everything else depends on.

  • Deep in security - access controls, PII protection, and compliance aren't an afterthought for you, they're a discipline

  • A driver of standards, not just a follower of them - you set the bar and hold teams accountable for meeting it, even when that means an uncomfortable conversation

  • Comfortable owning ambiguity - this role doesn't come with a fixed roadmap; you're helping define what "good" looks like here

OUR VALUES

People Analytics Analyst

About Us

ClearBank is a technology-enabled bank built to help transform banking and payments. We combine banking expertise and technology to provide infrastructure that enables our clients to deliver innovative financial products and services. Our culture is founded on trust, accountability, learning, collaboration and the confidence to challenge established ways of working responsibly.

We built ClearBank on the belief that banking infrastructure would no longer slow down progress. Instead, it would be a catalyst that unlocks the potential to innovate. It would adapt to different needs so a new era in financial services could begin. We’re here to challenge the status quo in banking, are you?

We all know that transforming banking forever is not an easy mission, but we’re more than ready to rise to that challenge. We all do it every day; navigating new, unexpected and sometimes even daunting challenges. But we believe in ourselves and trust we can do it. Want to innovate? Go for it. Push for a better way? You Can. If you think you have it in you, this is Where You Can.

The role:

Reporting to our Head of Reward, as the People Analytics Analyst you will help the People Team make informed, evidence-led decisions by turning data into clear, accurate and actionable insight.

Working across the People Team you will deliver reporting and analysis that supports organisational effectiveness, particularly focusing on Reward and People Operations among the wider team.

You will strengthen data quality, reporting controls and analytical capability across the People function, making insight easier to understand and use while protecting the confidentiality of employee information.

Key Responsibilities

  • Produce regular and ad hoc people reporting that gives stakeholders a clear view of workforce trends, risks and opportunities.

  • Analyse data across the employee lifecycle, including workforce composition, recruitment, retention, progression, performance, absence, engagement and inclusion.

  • Develop accessible dashboards, reports and visualisations that turn complex data into clear insights for People and business stakeholders.

  • Partner with Reward to support pay benchmarking, reward reviews, pay-positioning analysis and other compensation-related activity through accurate data preparation and analysis.

  • Maintain accurate and consistent people datasets, including clear data definitions, validation checks, reconciliation, documentation and version control.

  • Investigate data anomalies and work with People, Finance, Payroll and other stakeholders to resolve root causes and improve source-data quality.

  • Support workforce planning and organisational analysis by identifying patterns, modelling scenarios and presenting evidence-based observations.

  • Provide analytical support for People projects and recurring processes, ensuring outputs are accurate, timely and appropriate for their intended audience.

  • Improve reporting processes through automation, standardisation and the reduction of unnecessary manual activity.

  • Promote responsible use of people data by applying appropriate confidentiality, access, governance and quality controls.

What success looks like in the role:

  • Stakeholders receive accurate, timely and decision-ready people insights that help them understand workforce priorities and take appropriate action.

  • Core People reporting is supported by clear definitions, effective controls and reliable data that stakeholders trust.

  • People analytics increasingly covers the wider employee lifecycle, while Reward receives consistent and high-quality analytical support.

  • Recurring reports and processes become more efficient, scalable and easier to use through thoughtful automation and standardisation.

  • Complex findings are communicated clearly, with appropriate context, enabling stakeholders to understand both the evidence and its limitations.

Skills & Experience:

  • Experience in people analytics, HR reporting, workforce analytics, business analysis or another data-focused role.

  • Strong analytical and numerical skills, including experience working with detailed or complex datasets.

  • Ability to translate analysis into concise insights, clear visual outputs and practical recommendations.

  • Strong Excel capability, including formulas, data validation, reconciliation, data manipulation and structured analysis. Use or advocacy of AI is welcome.

  • Experience producing recurring reports, dashboards or management information for different stakeholder groups.

  • Strong attention to detail and a consistent approach to checking, documenting and controlling analytical outputs.

  • Understanding of data quality, confidentiality and the responsible handling of sensitive employee information.

  • Ability to investigate anomalies, identify root causes and work collaboratively with others to resolve data issues.

  • Strong planning and organisational skills, with the ability to manage recurring reporting alongside ad hoc analytical requests.

  • Clear communication and stakeholder-management skills, including the ability to explain analytical findings to non-technical audiences.

Nice-to-have

  • Experience working within a People or HR function in a regulated organisation, financial-services business or technology company.

  • Familiarity with HR information systems, reporting platforms or data-visualisation tools.

  • Experience supporting workforce planning, organisational design, employee-listening or inclusion analysis.

  • Exposure to reward analytics, salary benchmarking, pay-review modelling or compensation data.

  • Experience improving or automating reporting and data processes.

Ways of Working & Culture

  • Care like we mean it: Handle people data with care, respect and discretion, while producing insight that considers its impact on colleagues and the organisation.

  • Build trust together: Take ownership of data quality and delivery, follow through on commitments, exercise sound judgement and raise risks or limitations early.

  • Grow with the challenge: Stay curious, seek feedback and build analytical capability while adapting to changing priorities and new questions.

  • Succeed as one: Work collaboratively across People, Reward, Finance, Payroll and the wider business, engaging stakeholders early and focusing on shared outcomes.

  • Clear a bold new path: Challenge inefficient reporting practices, test better approaches and build solutions that can scale as the organisation’s analytical needs evolve.

Role Level: 2

If this sounds like you then we encourage you to dust off that CV and apply!

*Please note that we are not currently able to sponsor applicants for immigration purposes.

A little bit more about us! 

ClearBank is Where You Can belong: 

At ClearBank we think about Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DE&I) a lot. Not because we think we should. But because we know we should – how else can we build a happy workforce and be successful as a business. We’re committed to making sure our teams reflect society. And we put energy and effort into making this a place where everyone feels at home, where they’re given the trust and encouragement to do their very best work. Here are some of the things we’re most proud of: 

  • 42% of our senior management roles are held by women 

  • Our enhanced family leave policies

  • Launching our partnership with Code First Girls 

  • Increasing awareness of neurodiversity in the workplace through our partnership with the Inclusive Group 

Our hiring process and what you can expect:

Application: a member of our talent acquisition team will review your application against the key requirements for the role and let you know within two weeks whether you’re moving forward to the next stage; 

Screening: You’ll spend 30-45 minutes speaking to one of our recruiters learning more about the role and ClearBank, and we’ll get it know more about you, your experience and how your skills align with the role (this will be via phone or Teams video call). You can expect to hear back from us within seven days following this meeting (if things are taking longer than expected, we’ll let you know that too); 

First Interview: You’ll spend one hour with a member of our hiring team focusing on your skills, competencies and your ways of working at the same time we’ll give you time to ask more questions about the role, the team and learn more about the ClearBank culture. This will be via Teams.  

Second Interview: This will be a competency-based interview with one or more members of our team.

Final Stage: You will have a final meeting with the Head of Department. This will be around 45-60 minutes.  

Offer: Congratulations! Get ready to transform banking forever! 

 

Our commitment to you as a candidate: 

We will always try our best to get back to you within seven days of your interview whether you’ve been successful or not and provide you with feedback. Sometimes things take a little longer, so we may not have a decision to share but we will get it touch to let you know we need a little more time.  

We’re unable to provide specific individual feedback at the application or screening stage but know that your application was reviewed and considered carefully.  

We wish you the best of luck with your application and maybe we’ll be celebrating your new role at ClearBank soon!  

Equal Opportunities

ClearBank is committed to ensuring equal opportunities throughout every stage of the recruitment process. ClearBank recognises that diversity is vital to the long-term success of the business in the communities and markets in which it operates. ClearBank is also a firm believer that an inclusive culture fosters greater employee engagement and collaboration. 

ClearBank strives for diversity and inclusion of all forms, including (but not limited to): gender, age, educational and professional background, disability, gender reassignment, marital or civil partner status, pregnancy or maternity, race, colour, nationality, ethnic or national origin, religion or belief and sexual orientation. 

As part of the Company’s commitment to equal employment opportunity, we provide reasonable adjustments, to candidates during the recruitment process, including to individuals with disabilities. We want to create a safe space that welcomes everyone so please let us know how we can accommodate you. In case you have any accessibility requirements you can share that with our Talent Acquisition team prior to your interview stage, if applicable. 

The legal bit

By submitting your CV to ClearBank Limited you are providing your consent for us to use the information you provide for recruitment purposes. For more information on how we manage your data go and check out our Candidate Privacy Notice on the ClearBank website to see how we process, manage and look after your data. You are also allowing us to communicate with you by email and telephone for recruitment purposes.

Director of Communications – International Shows (Touring & Resident)
Sales, Marketing and Communications
Full-Time Position


Reports to: Reports to Vice President - Commercial, Europe, Middle East and Asia with a functional reporting line to SVP, Communication

Scope: All international shows outside the Americas (Europe, UK, Middle East, Africa, Asia-Pacific & Oceania) + Public Affairs
 
Teams: Touring show PR teams (embedded on tour) + Resident show PR teams, and their respective agency rosters
 
 
Role Purpose
 
The Director of Communications – International Shows (Touring & Resident) is responsible for driving demand, building anticipation, and ensuring cultural relevance for Cirque du Soleil’s shows across all markets outside the Americas.
 
This role elevates show communications into a strategic growth engine, integrating PR, earned media, and public affairs to create urgency, unlock market opportunities, and support commercial performance across every international production.
 
Based in London, this role acts as the central show communications and public affairs lead for international markets, ensuring alignment between show storytelling, market-level marketing plans, and cross-functional execution across multiple time zones, languages, and regulatory environments.
 
 
Core Mission
  • Drive anticipation, urgency, and sustained demand for international touring and resident shows
  • Make communications a core lever of the show marketing mix, fully integrated with paid, CRM, and ticketing
  • Lead, develop, and set standards for the touring and resident show PR teams and the agencies that support them
  • Own the strategy and governance of show-specific social media channels as an earned and owned demand driver
  • Leverage public affairs as a growth enabler to unlock market access, market entry, and partnerships
  • Ensure communications is a core driver of ticket revenue and brand equity outside the Americas
  • Orchestrate cross-functional alignment to deliver cohesive show launches across diverse international markets
Key Responsibilities
 
1. Show Communications Strategy – International Touring, Resident Shows & Public Affairs
  • Lead and oversee an international show communications strategy spanning touring productions, resident shows, and public affairs
  • Embed communications within the end-to-end demand engine (onsale → launch → sustain), in lockstep with market marketing plans
  • Integrate public affairs into market entry and growth strategies for new territories
  • Lead communications strategy in support of sponsorships and business development, including building relationships with key stakeholders, and developing joint communication plans with partners
2. Show Communications Leadership (Europe, UK, Middle East, Africa, APAC & Oceania)
  • Own communications strategy and performance across all international touring and resident productions
  • Ensure each show delivers:
    • Clear, differentiated narrative
    • Strong local and cultural relevance, adapted per market and language
    • Full lifecycle comms (pre-onsale → launch → sustain)
  • Implement standards, playbooks, and governance that scale across markets and local agency partners
  • Act as spokesperson for international shows and manage show-level issues in market, escalating to corporate communications at HQ where required
3. Show-Specific Social Media Ownership
  • Ensure each show PR team owns the strategy, management, and community engagement for its show-specific social media channels
  • Set the content, tone, and publishing standards that keep show channels distinctive while consistent with the masterbrand
  • Align show channel activity to the onsale, launch, and sustain calendar in each market
  • Drive creator, influencer, and talent-led content through show channels to build cultural relevance and organic reach
  • Set and track channel performance measures (growth, engagement, referral to ticketing) alongside earned media KPIs
  • Ensure coordination with central brand and social teams on shared assets, escalation paths, and community management protocols
4. Public Affairs & Stakeholder Engagement
  • Leverage public affairs as a strategic growth enabler by building relationships with:
    • Government and public sector stakeholders across international markets
    • Tourism boards, city partners, venues, and cultural institutions
  • Unlock opportunities to:
    • Support market entry for touring and resident shows
    • Facilitate partnerships and local integration
    • Strengthen Cirque du Soleil’s institutional influence outside the Americas
  • Coordinate closely with internal stakeholders to align on regulatory, reputational, and market access considerations, including visas, work permits, and cross-border touring requirements
5. Cross-Functional Orchestration
  • Own coordination across non-marketing functions to ensure aligned execution and messaging around shows, including:
    • Legal
    • HR (incl. talent mobility, immigration)
    • Sustainability
    • Operations
    • Sponsorship & partnerships
  • Act as the central orchestrator ensuring communications supports and amplifies show and market decisions
  • Ensure consistency between internal decisions, external messaging, and market execution, and act as the two-way bridge between international markets and HQ
6. Cultural Relevance & Media Impact
  • Position Cirque du Soleil’s shows as culturally relevant and premium in international markets
  • Build relationships with Tier 1 media, creators, and influencers across the UK, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific
  • Activate cultural moments and partnerships tied to international show launches and runs
7. Team Leadership, Agency Governance & Performance
  • Lead and develop the PR teams embedded with the touring shows and the PR teams responsible for the resident shows, across multiple markets, time zones, and languages
  • Build a consistent operating model, capability plan, and career path across both team groups, including onboarding for new tours and openings
  • Approve and sign off on all agency appointments, scopes, and budgets proposed by the touring and resident show PR teams
  • Define and manage the international agency ecosystem, setting selection criteria, performance standards, and review cadence
  • Set KPIs tied to business impact (demand, awareness, launch momentum, ticket sales, social channel performance)
  • Partner with marketing and analytics to link comms and social to revenue outcomes
Profile & Experience
 
Required
  • 10+ years in communications/PR with multi-market, international leadership experience
  • Proven ability to operate communications as a growth and demand lever tied to sales outcomes
  • Strong experience in consumer, brand, or entertainment PR, ideally with campaign or launch ownership
  • Experience working with government or public sector stakeholders in international markets
  • Deep media relationships across the UK and Europe, with demonstrated reach into additional international markets
  • Experience directly leading distributed, multi-time-zone in-house teams, including teams embedded with touring operations
  • Proven track record appointing, contracting, and managing PR agencies across multiple markets
  • Strong command of organic social media strategy and community management for consumer or entertainment brands
  • Ability to operate in a matrixed, cross-functional environment with a North America–based headquarters
  • Fluent in English (mandatory); willingness to travel frequently across international markets
Preferred
  • Additional language(s) relevant to key international markets (e.g. French, Spanish, German, Arabic, Japanese, Mandarin)
  • Experience in entertainment, touring productions, live events, or premium brands
  • Strong understanding of how communications integrates with marketing, CRM, and revenue generation

About Artificial

Help shape the future of specialty insurance

At Artificial, we’re building the next generation of technology for the specialty (re)insurance market. Our mission is to transform how brokers and carriers operate in complex markets by removing operational barriers and enabling smarter, faster decision-making.

We use modern technology to solve real challenges for some of the world’s leading brokers and insurers. By automating the repetitive and structuring the complex, we help our partners unlock new opportunities for innovation and growth.

You’ll be joining a collaborative team that values curiosity, ownership, and continuous learning. We work in an environment where ideas are heard, support is built-in, and outcomes matter. Everyone here has the chance to make a tangible impact on our products, our customers, and the industry.

We've just raised $45M (£33M) in Series B funding from lead investor CommerzVentures, new investor Move Capital, as well as all existing shareholders. This investment round gives us the room to grow with confidence, continue to innovate, and ensure that Artificial remains the first choice for brokers and carriers seeking a smarter way to trade digitally.

Join us, and take the chance to be a part of something that will change the landscape of insurance for generations.

About the Role

We are looking for a Quality Engineer to own test automation across Artificial's product platform. This is a hands-on technical role: we already have a substantial automated test suite - roughly 680 Playwright tests alone, plus extensive backend coverage - but it's grown quickly without a dedicated owner, and needs real structure, consolidation, and meaningful metrics built on top of it. You'll start on Platform, bringing structure to what exists and establishing standards for what gets added next, then extend automation into Transform/customer-configuration testing over time - an area with no automated coverage today, only manual execution by our existing testers, in work that's highly specific to each client.

Key Responsibilities

  • Reorganisation and consolidation: Bring coverage, completeness, and integrity to our existing ~680-test Playwright suite (plus extensive backend coverage) - identifying and removing duplication, fixing or removing flaky tests, and establishing clear structure and naming conventions where the suite has outgrown its original organisation

  • Meaningful metrics: Build real, trustworthy metrics off the back of the existing suite - coverage mapped to actual product routes and features (today's closest proxy, Playwright page objects, doesn't map cleanly to routes), pass/fail trends over time, and flaky-test tracking

  • Ongoing addition and maintenance: Own the suite as a living asset, not a one-off clean-up - adding new automated coverage as features ship, maintaining existing tests as the product changes, and keeping the suite healthy on an ongoing basis

  • CI pipeline scaling: The suite has grown 40% in three months (470 to 680 tests) and is now regularly hitting CI resource limits, with an 8-shard stress-test job approaching a 4-hour timeout. Work collaboratively with the QA Lead and Engineering on a real scaling plan for our existing CI pipeline (Buildkite) - this can't just mean adding more runners indefinitely. You'll be closely involved in shaping this, with full ownership expected to grow over time

  • Clarifying automation boundaries: Work with Engineering and FDE teams to establish a clear, documented relationship between platform-level automated tests and FDE "golden tests," removing current ambiguity about what covers what; also align with the performance testing work already underway so load/performance results sit in the same reporting picture rather than a separate silo

  • Mentorship: Support QA Engineers with automation as they need it - helping them write and troubleshoot tests, sharing what you know, and building their confidence over time

  • Reporting integration: Work with the QA Lead to integrate automated test results into the wider test management approach, so a test failure automatically generates a structured bug report linked back to Linear, rather than issues being created manually on an ad-hoc basis as they are today

  • Cross-team collaboration: Work closely with Engineering (who currently own significant existing automation) to agree a clear, documented handover and ongoing collaboration model, avoiding duplicated effort or unclear ownership

  • Building Transform/config automation from scratch: Once Platform is on a solid footing, extend automated coverage into FDE/customer-configuration testing - an area that has no automated coverage today, only manual execution by our existing testers. Unlike the Platform work above, this genuinely starts with nothing, in an area that's highly specific to each client rather than standard across the platform

About You

  • Strong hands-on experience building and owning test automation frameworks at scale, not just writing individual automated tests

  • Deep experience with Playwright, Cypress, or Selenium, including framework design and CI/CD integration

  • Comfortable working in or around a codebase - reading and reasoning about application code, even if not writing production features yourself

  • Experience diagnosing and resolving flaky or unreliable automated tests, and designing tests to avoid these problems from the start

  • Experience establishing test coverage visibility/reporting from scratch, where none previously existed - you'll use this directly when the role extends into Transform/config automation, which genuinely starts with nothing today

  • A methodical, standards-driven approach - you think about frameworks and patterns, not just individual test cases

Benefits

  • Private medical insurance

  • Income protection insurance

  • Life insurance of 4 * base salary

  • On-site gym and shower facilities

  • Enhanced maternity and paternity pay

Hi 👋 I’m Dom Allgood, Client Education Manager at hyperexponential. I joined four years ago as a Curriculum Developer and have spent the last couple of years growing Client Education into the (soon to be) five-person team it is today. Before hx I spent a decade teaching Computing in secondary schools. Outside of work most of my time goes to my two children, and what's left to running and, more recently, mountain biking - where I'm still very much a beginner.

Client Education exists to get our customers to value as quickly as possible, and to keep them there. We run instructor-led training, own hx Academy where all our self-paced learning content lives, own the certification programme, and run some of our customer events. We've also recently taken ownership of Developer+, and that's where this role comes in. Our first customers are working through the programme now, and as it grows it will need to evolve based on what we learn from them.

This isn't a typical Delivery Engineer role, you'll sit in Client Education rather than Delivery Engineering. You'll still work closely with the wider Delivery Engineering team, but your day to day is the customers on Developer+: delivering workshops, running drop-ins, reviewing their code, and shaping the programme around what you learn doing it. You'll partner with Product too, so customers can adopt new enhancements quickly and smoothly. There's no established playbook for this yet, so what matters most is the drive to build one. If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to own, I'd love to hear from you.

About hyperexponential (hx)

At hyperexponential, we're building the AI-powered platform that enables the world's most critical decisions in a £7 trillion industry: which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes — whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms.

Until now, insurance has been making billion-pound decisions using outdated tools. We're changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision — helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence.

Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we're scaling globally — already trusted by nearly 50 of the world's largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx.

What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do — from building the world's first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates.

What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn't tied to title or tenure; it's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure.

If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next.

About the Delivery Engineering team

The hyperexponential Delivery Engineering team is a unique blend of engineers, actuaries, mathematicians and data scientists. We don’t take on traditional “transformations” (we have brilliant partners for that) – we specialise in handling only the most difficult and interesting problems our customers face, where only a combination of technical depth, market expertise and hx knowledge will do.

The Delivery Engineering team are the experts' experts of the hx platform, knowing it top-to-bottom, inside-out – both breadth and depth. You’ll learn its limits and which can be pushed. You’ll uncover every trick in the book, the secret combinations, and the shortcuts. You’ll combine all of this with a growing knowledge of insurance technology to present 'the art of the possible' to our customers and help shape cutting-edge tech, while working alongside some of the brightest, most ambitious people in the tech and insurance industries.

What you'll be doing

  • Move customer teams from hx-led build to independent delivery, shifting effort from pairing toward review and advisory.

  • Keep every engagement moving to its prescribed path, sequencing services to each customer's build stage.

  • Deliver structured enablement sessions — architecture, coding best practice, testing and deployment, model lifecycles — pitched at each team's level.

  • Run code review as a consistent, standards-anchored service, evolving hx's model development standards where reviews expose gaps.

  • Provide drop-in support shaped by each customer's build stage, resolving most issues in session rather than escalating.

  • Make Developer+ repeatable rather than personality-dependent, documenting delivery and using AI to scale capacity.

  • Convert delivery knowledge into hx Academy content, prioritised by what reviews and drop-ins actually surface.

  • Act as the technical voice of the customer into Product, feeding back recurring friction on a regular rhythm.

What you'll need to have done

  • Built deep hx platform expertise and production-grade Python, including testing, deployment and model lifecycles.

  • Have excellent pricing and modelling judgement when working with customer’s - working with insurance & actuarial teams is a plus.

  • Developed strong technical enablement instincts, pitching sessions and documentation at the audience's real level.

  • Coached customer teams to work independently rather than solving problems for them.

  • Operated with high ownership and self-direction, building repeatable process where none exists.

  • Prioritised transparently across competing delivery, review and content demands.

  • Communicated with credibility and clarity across developers, actuaries, delivery partners and internal stakeholders.

You're unlikely to thrive here if

  • You prefer following detailed instructions rather than experimenting and finding your own approach.

  • You are uncomfortable working directly with non-technical stakeholders to understand their challenges.

  • You avoid tackling ambiguous or open-ended problems where the solution isn't obvious.

If reading our Culture Document leaves you feeling neutral rather than energised, hx may not be the place where you'll do your best work. We're building something that asks for commitment and conviction, and we want you to feel excited by the opportunity to grow with us.

Compensation

At hx, we're committed to salary transparency. You'll always have clarity on pay early in the process - our Talent Partner will share details with you during initial conversations - and we're working towards publishing salary information for all roles globally.

Because we're building at the intersection of technology/SaaS and insurance, our roles don't always map neatly onto traditional benchmarks. Our approach is to design compensation that's competitive in the market, fair across teams, and aligned with the impact our people make.

Equity: We offer equity across all roles at hx, making it a significant component of total compensation. Your Talent Partner will be able to share more details about this.

Benefits

£5,000 training and conference budget for individual and group development.

25 days of holiday plus 8 bank holidays (33 days total).

Company pension scheme via Penfold.

Mental health support and therapy via Spectrum.life.

Individual wellbeing allowance via Juno.

Private healthcare insurance through AXA.

Income protection and Life Insurance.

Cycle to Work Scheme.

Additional perks

Top-spec equipment (laptop, screens, adjustable desks, etc.).

Regular remote and in-person hackathons, lunch and learns, socials, and game nights.

Team breakfasts and lunches, snacks, drinks fridge, and a fun office at The Ministry.

Exceptional opportunities for personal development and growth as we build something remarkable together.

Interview process

  • Initial call with our Talent team

  • Take-home Python challenge followed by Skills Interview

  • Manager Interview

  • Values Interview

  • Meet the CEO

Our commitment to Diversity

hxers are at the centre of everything we build. We know that progress depends on diverse perspectives, and we are committed to creating an environment where everyone can thrive, grow, and make an impact. We recognise there is always more to do, and we take responsibility for shaping a workplace that is not only diverse but genuinely inclusive.

Diversity is not just the right thing to do, it is key to solving the complex challenges we choose to take on. By welcoming people from all backgrounds and experiences, we strengthen our ability to question assumptions, push boundaries, and design solutions that endure.

If you're energised by complexity and motivated to grow, we encourage you to apply and join our global team.

Next steps

If this opportunity resonates with you, we encourage you to apply or share it with your connections! Our dedicated talent team reviews all applications, and we promise to provide feedback regardless of the outcome.

data.description:
Orbital is the AI platform for real estate legal work.

Real estate shapes the world around us: our homes, our workplaces and our cultural landmarks. It’s the infrastructure that powers everyday life and is the world's largest asset class. Yet behind every single deal, real estate and legal teams work hard to navigate decades-old complexity; manually connecting documents, hidden obligations, geo-spatial context, and multiple parties into a path forward. We connect the legal and physical record, so that path is clearer than ever before. Our mission is to make real estate transactions faster, clearer, and less manual.

Here, you'll be part of changing how the deals behind the largest asset class get transacted, and will help shape the future of real estate.

A bit about us:

🚀 We’re building at the forefront of AI technology, without losing the deeply human expertise our clients depend on.

🏢 Orbital is built with former practising real estate lawyers and 250+ years of combined legal expertise. We're purpose-built for the complexity of real estate: accelerating due diligence, drafting and negotiation, and deal coordination with legal-grade precision.

💰 We've just raised a $60m Series B, led by Brighton Park Capital, to accelerate our global expansion – $75m raised to date.

🤝 We're trusted by 5,000+ real estate professionals, spanning UK Magic Circle and US Am Law 100 firms, to household names like M&S. Leading firms like BCLP, Orrick, Goodwin, Womble Bond Dickinson and Clifford Chance rely on Orbital to remove the busywork, freeing legal and real estate teams to focus on sharp judgment, standout client service, and closing deals faster.

💡 Working at Orbital means joining a bold, ambitious team, with the trust to take ownership and make a real impact from day one.

Role Overview 🔎

As a Senior UX Design Engineer, you'll own some of the hardest problems in our product and see them through until they're solved. You'll join our design team, three designers today and growing, and work inside our teams alongside product managers and our product, legal and AI engineers (our legal engineers are former real estate lawyers).

We've built a product that real estate lawyers rely on, and now we're also building for the businesses that own, occupy and develop property. You'll work across both, and much of it is new ground. Nobody here has the full answer yet, and that's the job: you'll get to know the people we build for, work out what they need from us, and build it.

This role is not about polishing screens. Our product is live and trusted by some of the most demanding real estate lawyers and property teams in the world. The hardest design problems here are not about how it looks. They are about whether people can trust it and get their work done.

Your starting point is the users, their work and the product: you notice what isn't working, decide what matters most, and see it through, from the first customer conversation to the version they use.

Here, designers build what they design. With AI coding tools, you'll build your designs into the product yourself, often live for customers the next day. When anyone can build, judgement matters most, and that is the heart of this role.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Find out who you're building for: talk to customers and map who does what inside law firms and property businesses. You'll do it together with the wider team.

  • Design how people work with our AI agents, which do real work on their behalf: what people hand over, how they check it and see where each answer came from, when they step in, what the agent asks about first and what it simply does, and how that shifts as AI improves.

  • Solve first, then refine: get to the right answer with rough, working versions in front of real people, and add polish once the problem is solved.

  • Build and ship interface changes yourself, using AI coding tools in our codebase. Engineering depth is welcome, not required.

  • Keep the product coherent while everyone builds: engineers, legal engineers, product people and coding agents all build interfaces here. Explain why one option beats another so people can make the call themselves, write it down as clear, reusable rules in the codebase for agents to follow, and evolve our design system so it all still feels like one product.


New to design engineering? 🌱

Design engineering is still a new kind of role, and most great candidates won't have had the title. If you're a strong designer with a good sense of product, and you're excited about building what you design, we'd love to hear from you. We'll help you make the shift.

You should apply if: ✍️

  • You go after the hard problem, not the surface one, and own it until it's solved. You judge your work by whether people use it, rely on it and come back.
